Aniline is a compound with the formula C6H5NH2. It consists of a benzene ring (which makes it aromatic) with an amino group (-NH2) attached directly to the ring. This structure classifies aniline as an aromatic amine.

Aromatic amines are a class of compounds that have an amino group (-NH2) attached directly to an aromatic ring (like benzene). The amino group contains nitrogen, and its attachment to the aromatic ring gives aniline its characteristic properties.

The other options:
- Aldehydes have a -CHO group
- Carboxylic acids have a -COOH group
- Ketones have a carbonyl group (C=O) bonded to two carbon atoms

Since aniline has an amino group attached to an aromatic ring, it belongs to the class of aromatic amines.
